It enshrines two deities, {{ill|Wakumusubi|ja|ワクムスヒ|mni|ꯋꯀꯨꯃꯨꯁꯨꯕꯤ|zh|和久產巢日神|qid=Q10921330|lt=Wakumusubi-no-Kami}} and {{ill|Toyouke-hime|Q2983724|qid=Q2983724|lt=Toyouke-bime-no-Kami}}. It is a candidate shrine for "Imaki Aoyasaka Inemi Shrine" of Kami District, {{ill|Musashi Province|ar|محافظة موساشي|ca|Província de Musashi|ckb|پارێزگای موساشی|cs|Provincie Musaši|de|Provinz Musashi|eo|Provinco Musaŝi|es|Provincia de Musashi|fa|ولایت موساشی|fr|Province de Musashi|gl|Provincia de Musashi|hak|Musashi-koet|id|Provinsi Musashi|it|Musashi (provincia)|ja|武蔵国|ko|무사시국|lt|Musašio žemė|nl|Musashi (provincie)|pl|Prowincja Musashi|pt|Província de Musashi|ru|Мусаси (провинция)|simple|Musashi Province|sk|Musaši (provincia)|sr|Провинција Мусаши|th|แคว้นมูซาชิ|tr|Musashi (vilayet)|uk|Провінція Мусаші|vi|Musashi (tỉnh)|zh|武藏國|zh_min_nan|Musasi-kok|zh_yue|武藏國|qid=Q907398}}, in the Engishiki. Former shrine rank: village shrine. It was the guardian shrine of old Gomyō village. {{nihongo|'''Tenjin-sha'''|天神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Musashi Province]].

== Origin ==
The founding date is unknown.
The shrine name is said to originate in rice-cultivation faith: immigrant-descended clans introduced advanced rice-growing techniques and enshrined the rice spirit<ref name="Tenjin-sha origin">Commemorative booklet for the 62nd Ise Grand Shrine rebuilding, ''Tenjin-sha Origin''</ref>. The immigrant-descended clans here refer to Imaki Kanjin, who came from Baekje on the Korean peninsula from the late 5th to early 6th century; because they migrated from their first settlement "Yamato no Kuni Imaki District," this is said to be the origin of the shrine-name element "Imaki."
<gallery widths="200px" heights="150px">
File:GomyouAma-jinja(Kamisato) Torii2.jpg|First torii
File:Ama-jinja(Kamisato,Gomyou) Torii1.jpg|Second torii
</gallery>
The current shrine buildings were rebuilt in 1722.
In 1832, Iwamatsu Manjirō of Nitta District, Kōzuke Province, donated a black-crested curtain and tall lanterns to Imaki Aoyasaka Inemi Daimyōjin<ref name="Kamisato board">Origin information board "Tenjin-sha" (installer: Kamisato Town, Saitama; installed March 1988)</ref>.
<gallery widths="200px" heights="150px">
File:GomyouAma-jinja(Misato) Haiden.jpg|Shrine buildings
File:GomyouAma-jinja(Misato) Kaguraden.jpg|Kagura hall
</gallery>
In 1967, a sacred stone rod inscribed:

''"emugi shikinai"''

''"imaki aoyasaka no kami"''

was discovered in the precincts. This became the basis for treating the shrine as a candidate for the Engishiki shrine name. Today this stone rod is enshrined as the sacred object<ref name="Kamisato board"/>.

== Precinct shrines ==
Merged in Meiji 10 (1877).
* Wakamiya Hakusan-sha<ref name="Kamisato board"/>

Merged in Meiji 42 (1909). Located behind the shrine buildings.
* Wakamiya Niu-sha<ref name="Kamisato board"/> (deity) Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto<ref name="Musashi villages">''Musashi no Kuni District/Village Records'' Vol.6, Hiraga District Gomyō Village (publisher: Saitama Prefecture, 1953)</ref>
: Founded in March of {{ill|Manju (era)|Q1194155|qid=Q1194155}} 1 (1024) by Fujiwara Tomochika.<ref name="Musashi villages"/>

Stone-hokora group on the right when facing the front of the haiden:
* Suwa Shrine / Inari Shrine / Yasaka Shrine / Ichikishima Shrine<ref name="Kamisato board"/>

== Events <ref name="Tenjin-sha origin" /> ==
* New Year Festival (Jan 1)
* Spring Festival (Mar 29)
* Great Purification Rite (Jul 31)
* Autumn Festival (Nov 19)
* Niiname Festival (Dec 9)

== Access ==
* From JR {{ill|Takasaki Line|Q1346657|qid=Q1346657}}{{ill|Jimbohara Station|Q845133|qid=Q845133}}, take Kamisato town bus {{ill|Komugicchi-go|Q28682946|qid=Q28682946}} (central route) bound for "Agri Park Kamisato" for 19 min. Get off at terminal "Agri Park Kamisato," then 15 min walk.
* 45 min on foot (3.3 km) from JR Takasaki Line Jinbohara Station
